title: HiLS Attention: Learning Chunk Selection for Near-Infinite Context
hook: Sparse attention never quite matched full attention because chunk selection was a heuristic. This version trains chunk selection end-to-end — then extrapolates 64x past its training length.
key_points: Dense attention's quadratic cost and poor length extrapolation motivate chunk-wise sparse attention, but prior methods fall short of full attention due to inaccurate chunk selection.

HiLS (Hierarchical Landmark Sparse) Attention factorizes attention hierarchically and folds chunk-retrieval scores directly into the forward pass, so they're optimized by the language-modeling loss itself — not a separate heuristic.
Matches or beats full attention at in-domain context lengths.
Extrapolates more than 64x the training context length while holding 90% retrieval accuracy — far beyond what full attention manages.
Existing full-attention models can convert to HiLS with lightweight continued pretraining, keeping in-domain performance while gaining ultra-long-context extrapolation.
content_html: Sparse attention promises to break the trade-off between context length and compute — skip the chunks that don't matter, keep only the relevant ones. In practice, every prior version has paid for that speed with accuracy, because deciding which chunks matter was never quite trained right.
extra_html: Hierarchical Landmark Sparse (HiLS) Attention factorizes attention hierarchically: each query attends independently to each retrieved chunk to pull out chunk-specific information, then fuses the results weighted by chunk-retrieval scores. The key move is folding those retrieval scores directly into the forward attention computation, so they get optimized by the language-modeling loss itself — end-to-end retrieval learning, not a bolted-on heuristic. The payoff shows up at both ends of the context-length spectrum: HiLS matches or beats full attention within the training context length, and extrapolates more than 64x beyond it while holding 90% retrieval accuracy, far past what full attention can do. Existing full-attention models don't need to be retrained from scratch either — lightweight continued pretraining converts them to HiLS, preserving in-domain performance while picking up the long-context extrapolation. Together, the sparse KV access and computation break the usual efficiency-versus-performance trade-off outright. Xiang Hu and colleagues, arXiv 2026 (34 HF community upvotes).

related.title: Ring Attention for Near-Infinite Context
related.hook: Spread one long sequence across many devices and compute attention blockwise - the context length you can handle grows with the number of devices, all with exact attention and no extra overhead.

related.title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
related.hook: Most tokens only need to look at their neighbors, so swap full attention for a sliding window plus a few global tokens and the cost goes from quadratic to linear in sequence length.

related.title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
related.hook: Split the difference between multi-head and multi-query attention: share KV heads across groups of query heads and get most of the memory savings with little quality loss.

flashcards.prompt: Why did prior chunk-wise sparse attention methods fall short of full attention, according to this paper?
flashcards.back_html: Their chunk selection was inaccurate — typically a separate heuristic not directly optimized by the training objective, so the model sometimes attended to the wrong chunks.

flashcards.prompt: What lets HiLS Attention learn accurate chunk selection, unlike prior sparse-attention methods?

choices.text: It incorporates chunk-retrieval scores directly into the forward attention computation, so they're optimized end-to-end by the language-modeling loss
It uses a much larger model to compensate for selection errors
It abandons sparsity and falls back to dense attention when accuracy drops
It relies on a human-labeled dataset of correct chunk selections

flashcards.explanation_html: By fusing retrieval scores into the forward pass, HiLS lets the LM loss directly train which chunks to attend to — end-to-end retrieval learning — rather than bolting a heuristic selector onto attention after the fact.
